topics.title: Antarctic sea ice hits third-lowest winter maximum
topics.summary: A new report says Antarctic sea ice reached its third-lowest winter maximum in 2026, extending a steep decline after years of unusually high ice coverage. Scientists are tracking whether the shift marks a lasting change in Antarctic sea ice conditions.
topics.detail: The report says the 2026 winter peak covered about 17.59 million square kilometers. It says this was the third-lowest winter maximum in the satellite record. The article says researchers are continuing to monitor whether the decline is a long-term transformation or part of natural variability.

sources.title: Antarctica's sea ice has undergone a stunning reversal

topics.title: Urban cycling worlds in Riyadh are cancelled
topics.summary: The UCI has cancelled the Urban Cycling World Championships that were set for Riyadh from November 3 to 7. The decision followed a week of attacks on Riyadh airport, according to the report.
topics.detail: The event had been scheduled to run in Saudi Arabia in early November. The article says the cancellation was announced after attacks on the airport in Riyadh. No replacement venue or revised dates were reported.

sources.title: The Urban Cycling World Championships in Riyadh have been cancelled

topics.title: Kilauea stays at watch level after eruption ends
topics.summary: The U.S. Geological Survey said Kilauea was at WATCH level on October 14, and later said the volcano remained at advisory status on October 17. A separate update said episode 55 of the ongoing Halemaʻumaʻu eruption ended abruptly on October 17.
topics.detail: The USGS notice said Kilauea was at WATCH in the October 14 update. The later volcano updates page said the alert level was ADVISORY and that episode 55 ended at 9:03 a.m. HST on October 17. The same page said monitoring data remained consistent with background activity levels in the Cascade Range, but that was a separate update.

sources.title: Volcano Updates | U.S. Geological Survey - USGS.gov

topics.title: Ukrainian scientists begin new Antarctic season
topics.summary: The Ukrainian research vessel Noosphere has sailed from Cape Town to Antarctica, starting the sixth Antarctic season of the Ukrainian expedition. Scientists plan work in the Weddell Sea with Swedish colleagues, along with logistics stops at Polish and Chilean stations.
topics.detail: The report says the Noosphere will first stop at the Polish Antarctic station Arctowski. It then will head to Punta Arenas to collect Ukrainian seasonal researchers and cargo for the Akademik Vernadsky station. The season’s planned work includes studies of extremophile organisms near hydrothermal vents, cold-water corals, atmospheric rivers, ocean currents, and a sunken ship.

sources.title: Ukrainian scientists will search for a sunken ship and coral reefs in Antarctica
